input: I stand with Aldric. "I can certainly be grateful for a safe arrival. You may have to forgive me the words; I don't know yours yet." I follow the offered thanks without pretending to a prayer I don't know, then take the seat marked for me. "And thank you for putting my name down. I was worried choosing a chair would be my first examination."
output:
Aldric’s formal expression softens by a degree. “Honesty is no insult to the Light.”

At his lead, the table rises. Ashara does so with the look of someone tolerating a necessary drill; Rashid’s bow is exact. Ysolde merely inclines her white head. Thessaly remains seated, hands folded beside her place setting, while Seraphel stands with her small wings tucked close.

Aldric holds his palms upward over the candles. “Divine Light, witness those who have crossed thresholds safely. Give us clear judgment, restraint in power, and peace worthy of the cost that made it.”

Seraphel answers quietly,

“Let no bright vow become a chain;  
Let strangers find their names again.”

For a moment, only the lamps hum.

Then chairs draw back. A server ladles pale gold soup into your bowl, fragrant with roasted root vegetables, pepper, and something sharp enough to wake the tongue. The seat proves less ceremonious than feared, though its high back bears a deeply carved Garvey crest.

At your remark, Thessaly examines the empty chairs farther down the table. “Choosing an unmarked one would have been difficult. Most are assigned to people who are not here.”

“That sounds ominous,” Rashid says, taking his seat.

“It is not intended to.”

Ysolde settles beside you with almost no rustle of fabric. “The chair examination occurs later,” she says. Her grey eyes stay quite level. “It is famously cruel.”

Ashara lets out a short laugh before reaching for bread. “Don’t encourage him.”

Caelindra has not touched her spoon. Silver hair falls over one shoulder like poured metal as she looks at you across the candlelight. “Did the lawyers at least explain why they had sent a human heir to a house full of people expected to become diplomatic incidents?”
